title: A uniformly squeezed Gaussian has an exact quartic-scale coefficient functional

uniform_squeeze.trial: For fixed 0<s<=1 set every real covariance eigenvalue s_j=s and optimize the constant physical mean y_N=a_N^2 over y_N>=0
uniform_squeeze.finite_cutoff_optimizer: Including the zero-mode coherent cost (m^2/2)y_N, the exact optimizer is y_N=[3C_N(1-s)-m^2/(4g)]_+ rather than the interaction-only optimizer
uniform_squeeze.finite_cutoff_interaction: The exact K1524 Wick polynomial is y_N^2-6C_N(1-s)y_N+C_N^2(3s^2-6s+9)
uniform_squeeze.finite_cutoff_total: Writing B_N=Omega_N, the optimized total is (B_N/4)(s+s^(-1)-2)+gC_N^2(3s^2-6s+9)-[6gC_N(1-s)-m^2/2]_+^2/(4g)
uniform_squeeze.leading_functional: For fixed g>0 and fixed 0<s<=1, y_N/C_N tends to 3(1-s) and N^(-4)Rayleigh_N(s) tends to e_g(s):=(c_Omega/4)(s+s^(-1)-2)+6g c_C^2 s(2-s)
uniform_squeeze.endpoint: At s=1 the trial is the vacuum and e_g(1)=6g c_C^2; as s tends to zero the squeeze term diverges
uniform_squeeze.scope_guard: The formula is exact only for the declared translation-invariant uniform-squeeze Gaussian family; it is an upper-trial coefficient, not the unrestricted ground-energy coefficient or an O(1) recentering
